Ancient History.Prehistoric India:
INTRODUCTION
Prehistory denotes the period before the emergence of writing and literary records. Knowledge of this phase is reconstructed entirely through archaeological evidence such as stone tools, faunal remains, plant residues and rock art. It represents the longest phase of human existence and marks the gradual evolution of human subsistence, technology and social organisation.

PALEOLITHIC AGE
The Paleolithic phase marks the earliest stage of human history characterised by a food gathering economy and rudimentary technology. It extended roughly from 2.5 million years ago to about 10000 BCE and reflects adaptation to harsh climatic conditions of the Ice Age.

FEATURES
• Dominance of hunting and gathering as the primary mode of subsistence
• Use of core and flake tools such as hand axes, cleavers and choppers made mainly of quartzite
• Absence of permanent settlements with a nomadic way of life
• Gradual control over fire in later stages which enabled cooking and protection
• Development of tool typology leading to division into Lower, Middle and Upper Paleolithic phases

The Lower Paleolithic is associated with large bifacial tools, while Middle Paleolithic shows flake tools and Upper Paleolithic reflects improved blade technology and artistic expressions.

IMPORTANT SITES
• Bhimbetka rock shelters provide evidence of continuous human occupation and early artistic activity
• Hunsgi valley shows habitation patterns linked to water sources
• Kurnool caves indicate early human adaptation to cave environments
• Belan valley reflects long cultural sequence from Paleolithic onwards

MESOLITHIC AGE
The Mesolithic phase represents a transitional stage marked by climatic improvement after the Ice Age and gradual diversification of subsistence strategies. It broadly dates between 10000 BCE and 6000 BCE.

FEATURES
• Extensive use of microliths which were often hafted onto wood or bone to form composite tools
• Beginning of semi sedentary life with seasonal settlements
• Domestication of animals such as dog indicating closer human animal interaction
• Evidence of fishing, hunting of smaller animals and gathering of plant resources
• Burials with grave goods indicating emergence of belief systems

This phase reflects adaptation rather than a complete break from Paleolithic traditions, with increasing control over environment.

IMPORTANT SITES
• Bagor provides earliest evidence of animal domestication in India
• Langhnaj shows hunting and pastoral activities
• Sarai Nahar Rai gives evidence of human burials and social practices
• Adamgarh reflects continuity of microlithic culture

NEOLITHIC AGE
The Neolithic phase marks a fundamental transformation in human history with the beginning of food production. It developed at different times in different regions of the Indian subcontinent, roughly from 6000 BCE onwards.

FEATURES
• Shift from food gathering to agriculture and animal domestication
• Use of polished stone tools indicating technological advancement
• Emergence of permanent settlements and village communities
• Development of pottery, weaving and storage practices
• Increasing social organisation and division of labour

Unlike earlier phases, humans began modifying nature rather than merely adapting to it.

IMPORTANT SITES
• Mehrgarh represents one of the earliest agricultural settlements with evidence of wheat and barley cultivation
• Burzahom is known for pit dwellings and unique burial practices
• Chirand shows early farming and animal husbandry in eastern India
• Hallur indicates Neolithic expansion into South India

SIGNIFICANCE
The prehistoric phase marks the most crucial transition in human history from a passive dependence on nature to an active control over resources. The shift to agriculture laid the foundation for surplus production, population growth and the emergence of complex societies. These developments ultimately paved the way for the rise of urban civilisations such as the Indus Valley Civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS
• Stone tool typology is the primary basis for classification of prehistoric phases
• Microliths are the defining feature of Mesolithic culture
• Neolithic phase is associated with agriculture but it did not develop uniformly across regions
• Mehrgarh provides earliest evidence of farming in the subcontinent

PYQ TRAP
Questions often confuse features of Paleolithic and Neolithic phases. Agriculture, permanent settlement and polished tools belong only to the Neolithic phase, whereas Paleolithic is strictly a hunting gathering stage.
